title: Introduce stream sync heuristic and delimiter damping to reduce partial-JSON churn
author: Priya Rao
description:
Context and motivation: We continue to see production noise from repeated delimiter emission and mid-stream partial-JSON bursts under variable network conditions. This causes downstream OpenAI-compat layers and SDK consumers to reparse/repair fragments frequently, increasing CPU and spurious function-call ordering anomalies. The goal of this PR is to reduce churn at the protocol boundary by introducing a lightweight stream sync heuristic combined with a delimiter-damping window that suppresses noisy delimiter repetition while preserving strict event ordering and function/tool-call semantics.

What changed (high level): 1) delimiter_damping: a short-time-window dampener that collapses repeated stream terminators (",\n\n"/"\n") emitted in rapid succession into a stable single terminator plus a compact marker. This is intentionally conservative: we only collapse when sequence IDs and token cursors indicate no intervening payload could have been lost. 2) sync heuristic: compute a trailing-kv-length fingerprint and seq-ack delta over the last N fragments. When the heuristic detects stable ack progression, we allow coalescing and a small reordering tolerance for heartbeats. 3) function-call handoff: ensure that tool/function call sentinel ordering is maintained by adding a final flush-to-epoch barrier before emitting a functioncall sentinel; this prevents off-by-one cases where a delimiter coalescer delayed earlier bytes. 4) compatibility adapter: small changes to openai_compat stream adapter to accept the compact marker and resume reassembly without triggering a partial-JSON repair path.

Commits (summary):
- 1a3f2b5 introduce delimiter damping module and tests
- 2c7d9e4 add trailing-kv-length sync heuristic and integration with parser
- b4f88d1 adjust functioncall flush ordering and add epoch barrier
- d9e2ab0 update openai_compat adapter to recognize compact marker and resume
- 8c6f0e7 add benchmarks and regression tests for partial-JSON scenarios

Files touched (high level):
- server/streaming/parser.rs (new damping + heuristic hooks)
- server/streaming/heuristics/damping.rs (core algorithm and tests)
- server/streaming/heuristics/sync.rs (trailing-kv fingerprint logic)
- sdk/openai_compat/stream_adapter.py (compact marker handling)
- bench/streaming/partial_json_bench.py (bench harness and datasets)
- server/streaming/tests/test_partial_json_reassembly.rs (integration tests)
- docs/streaming/damping-notes.md (design rationale and configuration)

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for the damping module and sync heuristic. Integration tests replicate upstream partial-JSON scenarios recorded from PROD incident logs (SUP-883). Benchmarks show ~48% reduction in reparsing events on a simulated 100ms jitter path, and a 12% CPU reduction in the OpenAI-compat adapter under heavy burst traffic. The CI run initially failed one flake (async test timeout) on macOS runners; reran the job and green across all matrices._CI details: build ↦ pass, unit-tests ↦ pass, integration-tests ↦ pass, lint ↦ pass.

Review thread summary:
- Ethan: asked for proof that coalescing doesn't mask genuine loss — provided the sync fingerprint checks and updated comments. Requested that the damping window be configurable at runtime (added via parser config).
- Maya: requested a microbenchmark for functioncall ordering — added bench and synthetic test. Also asked for a clear fallback path if the compact marker is unrecognized by older clients (added a compatibility parity mode that emits both traditional delimiter + marker for one epoch).
- Lucas: questioned safety of collapsing newlines when UTF-8 sequences span fragments — added explicit UTF-8 boundary checks and tests for split-UTF8 sequences.
- Author replies: clarified heuristics, added comments, and tightened gating conditions. All reviewers approved after two iterations.

Notes on rollout and ops: default damping window set to 80ms and can be tuned via the stream_parser.damping.window_ms flag in the config. The rollout plan is canary to 5% for 24h with enhanced observability (emit "damping.event" metric and "sync.heuristic.score" histogram). If any increase in client-side repair rates is observed, we will revert via feature flag.

Release notes: Reduce partial-JSON reparsing and improve stability of SSE streaming by collapsing noisy delimiters and adding a stream-sync heuristic. Backwards compatible; safe default.

Related work: builds on prior stream-resync and fragment-checkpoint efforts (see ENG-2141 and PRs that introduced span checkpoints), but differs by focusing on short-term delimiter noise suppression and a lightweight trailing fingerprint instead of heavy checkpointing.
